title: Bind the orchestrator settings to the typed approval policy
description:
CONSUMER EDGE for task-5d8f11c86a3a41b4a8a420ef0d52a444. Clause 1 requires this task to exist. This is the consumer closest to the incident that motivated the contract.

THE INCIDENT, stated exactly, because it is what this task prevents recurring. On 2026-08-15 the orchestrating board ran auto-approval on a 2s delay configured OUTSIDE any typed contract — a setting nobody had stated per unit of work. Every BLOCKED task was promoted to PLANNING inside a two-minute window, clearing each task's recorded blockedReason. Two were release-cutover tasks whose descriptions named an explicit human authority gate as a hard dependency: a GA activation record requiring GO_ACTIVATE, and a legacy quiesce drill requiring GO_QUIESCE. Neither GO had ever been issued — verified by scanning every message channel. Both became claimable under that 2s delay, so no human would have seen a plan before a worker began executing it.

WHAT LANDED (commit 18f0964, published from the @moe/core root, verify by grep before naming symbols):
- APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS, frozen: ["PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN", "REQUIRE_HUMAN"].
- ApprovalPolicy, a discriminated union whose PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN arm carries a REQUIRED delayMs. It is deliberately impossible to express an auto-approval policy without stating its delay — that is the whole point, and it is exactly the property the untyped setting lacked.
- decideApprovalAuthority, HumanAuthorityGate, grantHumanAuthority, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS.

SCOPE: decode the orchestrator's approval settings into a typed ApprovalPolicy, refusing rather than defaulting when the delay is absent or malformed. NOT IN SCOPE: the daemon wiring (task-5fcfdae58ec7419fbcba0000ef08d3b6), the control-room surface (task-6fcca7da2bc44194b36bb2454088a62b), or changing the contract.

DO NOT MAKE THE SETTING THE GATE. A blanket project-wide switch is what FAILED in the incident, and the contract's rails say so: fast delegation was the correct setting for most of that board, and flipping everything to manual review to protect two tasks is the wrong trade. This task binds the POLICY. The gate is per-unit-of-work and is not expressible in, or satisfiable by, a settings file — if the design lets a settings value approve gated work, the design is wrong.

A DECODE THAT DEFAULTS IS THE DEFECT. An absent delay must produce a refusal with a stable code, not a fallback value. `mem:pinned-value-is-a-decision-only-if-another-was-representable` — a decoder that cannot express "refuse" makes every decoded delay meaningless.
definitionOfDone: The orchestrator's approval settings decode into a typed ApprovalPolicy from @moe/core, with the decode reachable from the settings load path rather than only exported.

An absent, empty, or malformed auto-approval delay is REFUSED with an exact stable code and its layer, asserted literally - never defaulted to a fallback delay. A test proves the refusal is representable by showing a valid settings value decoding successfully in the same suite.

No settings value, or combination of them, approves gated work; a test enumerates every ApprovalPolicy member decodable from settings against a gated unit and asserts refusal for each, with a nonzero exact cardinality equal to the vocabulary size.

The settings binding introduces no project-wide switch that stands in for the per-unit-of-work gate, and a test asserts a gated unit stays refused under the most permissive settings the file can express.
A mutation drill making the decoder default an absent delay instead of refusing turns a named test red on its code-and-layer assertion, restored byte-exact and verified by hash.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE, AND READ THE LIVE DEFECT THIS TASK ACTUALLY CLOSES. The human's decision was "apps/daemon grows the loader plus a real call site". Measuring for that found the call site ALREADY EXISTS and is currently sourcing its policy wrongly — which makes this a repair, not a greenfield add. Confirm all of this at current HEAD (measured at 0f19e06) before writing anything.
`apps/daemon/src/planning/planning-services.ts` already imports `decideApprovalAuthority` and `ApprovalPolicy` from `@moe/core` (:2,:4) and calls it at :192-194 with `policy: approvalPolicy(request.payload)`. That helper (:139-146) reads `payload["approvalPolicy"]`, returns `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` when absent, and otherwise CASTS the caller's object through `as unknown as ApprovalPolicy` with no validation. `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` (:134) is `{kind: "PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN", delayMs: 0}`.
NOW THE PART THAT MAKES IT LIVE: `PAYLOAD_KEYS["approval.decide"]` (daemon-command-registry.ts:98) is `["activation", "command", "graphRevisionRef", "record", "runId"]` — `approvalPolicy` is NOT allow-listed, and the seam refuses a payload carrying a disallowed key rather than trusting it (:194). So `value === undefined` is ALWAYS true and `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` is the policy for EVERY gate-free approval decision in the daemon today: proceed without a human, immediately, with a delay nobody stated.
That is verbatim the incident `@moe/core`'s own contract comment describes at approval-policy.ts:47-52 — "An auto-approval delay that defaults implicitly is the incident's actual mechanism: that board ran a 2s auto-approval nobody had stated per unit of work." Read that comment before designing the loader; it is the specification.
Also note the caller-cast path is currently unreachable but NOT harmless: it is one allow-list edit away from letting a client self-approve. This task removes it rather than relying on a guard in a different file.
DO NOT re-derive the ruled-out carriers. `ProjectConfigurationSettings` (packages/contracts/.../project-configuration-contract.ts:154) and `WrapperKnobs` (orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.ts:9) were both measured and ruled out three times; they carry no approval mode.
GATES, each run separately with its own exit code — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, recording the count line and every failing file as your before-set. Both expected RED from foreign slices; repair none of it.

TDD RED, PART 1 — the loader, which must fail closed in every direction. Create the loader's test against the not-yet-existing module. The loader turns daemon settings into an `ApprovalPolicy` from `@moe/core`, whose closed vocabulary is `APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS` = `["PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN", "REQUIRE_HUMAN"]` (approval-policy.ts:36) and whose `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN` arm REQUIRES `delayMs` by construction.
MAPPING TO PIN: an approval mode naming SPEED, together with an explicitly stated non-negative integer delay, yields `{kind: "PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN", delayMs}` carrying THAT delay. Everything else yields `{kind: "REQUIRE_HUMAN"}`. "Everything else" is the whole point, so sweep it and assert a positive generated-case count: settings absent; approval mode absent; an unrecognised mode; SPEED with the delay ABSENT; SPEED with a non-integer, negative, NaN, Infinity or non-number delay; a delay supplied as a numeric string.
SPEED-WITHOUT-A-DELAY MUST BE `REQUIRE_HUMAN`, NOT A DEFAULTED NUMBER. The contract says "a policy that cannot be constructed without naming its delay cannot hide one" — substituting any default here re-creates the incident in a new place. Assert that no code path can produce `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN` without an explicitly stated delay.
Assert the direction of every refusal too: there must be NO input, malformed or otherwise, for which the loader answers `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN`. Write that as a property over the whole swept set, not a per-case check — a per-case list can be extended with a permissive case and stay green.
Where the loader reads from is a design choice this task makes: follow the daemon's established config precedent (`readStoreDependencyEnv`, daemon-store-dependencies.ts:45, and `readWrapperKnobs`) rather than inventing a new mechanism, and state the source in the module header so it is auditable.

TDD RED, PART 2 — the call site, including a regression test for the defect measured in step 1. In `planning-services.ts`'s test:
(a) THE REGRESSION: with settings that do NOT authorise auto-approval, an `approval.decide` for gate-free work must NOT proceed without a human. Today it does — `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` makes every such decision `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN` at 0ms — so this test MUST FAIL before the fix. Verify it reddens against current HEAD before implementing; a regression test that passes today is testing nothing.
(b) With settings that DO authorise it, the decision proceeds and carries the STATED delay — assert the exact configured number reaches `ApprovalAuthorityDecision.delayMs`, not merely that some delay is present.
(c) A satisfied human gate still proceeds with `delayMs: 0` and carries the grant, per `decideApprovalAuthority` (:127-137) — the loaded policy must not disturb the gate path, since satisfying a gate takes a named human principal and is not a policy value.
(d) NO POLICY CAN COME FROM THE PAYLOAD. Assert that a payload carrying an `approvalPolicy` key cannot change the decision, and that the handler exposes no path that reads one. The registry allow-list already refuses that key today, but this assertion must hold at the HANDLER, so the guarantee survives an allow-list edit in a different file.
(e) THE TIMER BOUND. `ApprovalAuthorityDecision.delayMs` is documented as a safe non-negative integer, WIDER than `setTimeout` accepts: "A delay above 2**31-1 CLAMPS to 1ms there, so a consumer that means 'effectively never' and passes it straight to a timer gets 'immediately' — the inversion this contract exists to prevent. Bound it at the consumer, where the timer lives." Assert a delay above 2**31-1 does NOT become an immediate proceed. This is the single nastiest failure mode in the task: the inversion turns the most conservative configuration into the most permissive one.

IMPLEMENT THE LOADER. Create `apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-policy-settings.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./approval-policy-settings.ts";`, LF ending — apps/daemon requires a physical bridge per production module and the guard byte-compares, so CRLF or a trailing blank line lands it in `wrongContent`).
It reads the daemon's approval settings and returns an `ApprovalPolicy` typed against `@moe/core` — import the type from the BARE specifier, do not restate the union locally. Construct `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN` only from an explicitly stated non-negative safe integer delay; every other input, including a missing delay, returns `REQUIRE_HUMAN`.
Write the fail-closed direction into the module header WITH its reason, citing approval-policy.ts:47-52: an implicitly defaulted delay is the incident's mechanism, so this loader has no default delay and no permissive fallback. A future reader who sees `REQUIRE_HUMAN` returned for a malformed setting must be able to tell it is deliberate rather than an oversight to "fix".
Do NOT modify `packages/core/**`. `decideApprovalAuthority`, `APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS` and the `ApprovalPolicy` mapped type are complete and separately tested; if the contract genuinely cannot express the mapping, report blocked rather than editing it.
Keep the module under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts). Do NOT publish from apps/daemon/src/index.ts — index-surface.test.ts pins an exact export count and index.ts is not an owned path here.

REPLACE THE POLICY SOURCE, AND DELETE THE OLD ONE. In `planning-services.ts` (221 lines):
(1) Source the policy from the loader at :192-194, replacing `policy: approvalPolicy(request.payload)`.
(2) DELETE `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` (:134-137) and the `approvalPolicy(payload)` helper (:139-146) outright. Do not keep either as a fallback. A payload-sourced or defaulted policy must become UNREPRESENTABLE in this handler, not merely unreachable — the current unreachability depends on an allow-list in a different file, and this task's whole point is that authority should not rest on a distant guard.
(3) BOUND THE DELAY WHERE THE TIMER LIVES, per the contract's explicit instruction. `delayMs` is a safe non-negative integer, wider than `setTimeout`; a value above 2**31-1 clamps to 1ms and inverts "effectively never" into "immediately". Clamp or refuse at this consumer, and say which in a comment.
The handler must keep failing closed on every existing arm — do not let the loader's refusal path change which layer answers an unrelated refusal. `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES` and `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS` (approval-authority.ts:34,46) are unchanged and every existing refusal keeps its exact code and layer.
Measure the file after editing with `grep -c ''`; deleting two blocks and adding one call should shrink it, but confirm rather than assume.

MUTATION DRILLS — prove the fail-closed direction is real and not incidental. Run each alone, revert before the next. (1) RESTORE `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` as the fallback when settings are unreadable; the step-3(a) regression test MUST redden — this is the drill for the live defect, and if it stays green the regression test never exercised the defect at all. (2) Make the loader default a missing delay to any number while keeping `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN`; the SPEED-without-delay case must redden — proving the contract's "cannot be constructed without naming its delay" is enforced here rather than assumed from the type. (3) Remove the consumer-side delay bound and pass `delayMs` straight to the timer; the 2**31-1 case must redden — and note it must redden on the INVERSION (an immediate proceed), not merely on a wrong number. (4) Re-add a payload read for `approvalPolicy`; the no-policy-from-payload case must redden at the HANDLER, proving the guarantee does not depend on the registry allow-list. (5) Make one loader refusal answer `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN`; the whole-set property assertion must redden — proving that property is a real sweep and not a list of hand-picked cases.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Confirm each red lands on the INTENDED assertion, not an unrelated crash or compile error. Restore with `git checkout -- <the one drilled file>` (never by hand) and verify `git status --short` shows it clean before the next; a foreign whole-tree completion hook can otherwise commit a drill left on disk.

GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT. Legs, each run separately with its own captured exit code — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, then `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` reading the `Test Files`/`Tests` COUNT LINE rather than the exit code (exit 0 with no count line ran nothing). Both stay RED from the foreign slices recorded in step 1. Apply the path-attributed baseline — HEAD failing paths minus merge-base failing paths, intersected with your owned files, MUST be empty — and quote the remaining foreign red verbatim.
PROVE THE GAP CLOSED: `grep -rn "approvalMode\|speedModeDelayMs" --include=*.ts apps packages` now returns production hits where it returned ZERO before — that grep has been the standing unblock test across three prior audits, so quote it.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: (a) is `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` GONE, not merely unused — `grep` it and expect nothing? (b) is `approvalPolicy(payload)` gone, so a payload-sourced policy is unrepresentable at the handler rather than blocked by a distant allow-list? (c) can ANY input produce `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN` without an explicitly stated delay? (d) is `delayMs` bounded where the timer lives, with the 2**31-1 inversion covered? (e) does a satisfied human gate still proceed at `delayMs: 0` carrying its grant, unchanged? (f) is `packages/core/**` untouched? (g) does every existing refusal keep its exact `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES` member and layer? (h) is the loader under 250 lines by `grep -c ''`, the bridge one LF line, index.ts unmodified? (i) does `git status --porcelain` show only owned paths with every drill reverted?
Commit by explicit pathspec naming each owned file — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`; the index is shared state in this single working directory. Verify with `git show --stat`. In the completion: quote the count lines and the closing grep verbatim, name the test that reddened for each drill, and STATE THE DEFECT THIS CLOSED — that before this task every gate-free approval decision in the daemon used `{kind:"PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN", delayMs:0}`, because the payload key that could override it was never allow-listed. That is the finding QA should verify, not just the loader's existence. Keep verification.command under 500 characters.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 7 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Build a loader and leave `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` as a fallback for unreadable settings. REJECTED, and it is the most likely wrong implementation because it looks defensive: the default IS the defect. An unreadable setting must yield `REQUIRE_HUMAN`, never a permissive default. Drill 1 restores the fallback and requires the regression test to redden.

2) Keep `approvalPolicy(payload)` and rely on the registry allow-list to block it. REJECTED: the guarantee would live in a different file from the handler that depends on it, and one allow-list edit re-opens self-approval. Delete the branch so a payload-sourced policy is unrepresentable here.

3) Default a missing `speedModeDelayMs` to some number when the mode says SPEED. REJECTED by the contract's own words — a policy that cannot be constructed without naming its delay cannot hide one. Substituting a default re-creates the incident one layer out. SPEED-without-a-delay is `REQUIRE_HUMAN`.

4) Pass `delayMs` straight to `setTimeout`. REJECTED: above 2**31-1 it clamps to 1ms, inverting the most conservative setting into an immediate proceed. The contract says bound it at the consumer; drill 3 requires the red to land on the inversion specifically.

5) Add the approval settings to `ProjectConfigurationSettings`. REJECTED: that is the product configuration manifest with its own digest and selection path; extending it for a transitional daemon setting couples two lifecycles, and it was already ruled out three times as a carrier.

6) Change `packages/core`'s contract to accept a mode string directly. REJECTED: the contract is complete and its exhaustiveness anchor is deliberate. The mapping from settings to policy is the daemon's job, which is exactly what the human's option (a) assigns here.

7) Land the loader now and wire the call site in a follow-up. REJECTED and explicitly foreclosed by the human's decision: loader plus call site in the same task, so Clause 1 is satisfied by a genuine consumer edge rather than an export-only module.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 0f19e06, after the human answered my escalated (a)/(b)/(c) question with option (a). Planning it under that decision found something the three prior audits did not: THE CALL SITE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS SOURCING ITS POLICY WRONGLY, so this is a repair of a live authority defect rather than a greenfield add.

THE DEFECT, measured. `apps/daemon/src/planning/planning-services.ts` (221 lines) already imports `decideApprovalAuthority` and `ApprovalPolicy` from `@moe/core` (:2,:4) and calls it at :192-194 with `policy: approvalPolicy(request.payload)`. That helper (:139-146):
  `const value = payload["approvalPolicy"]; if (value === undefined) return DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY; if (object) return value as unknown as ApprovalPolicy; return {kind:"INVALID_POLICY"} as unknown as ApprovalPolicy;`
and `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` (:134) is `{kind: "PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN", delayMs: 0}`.

WHY IT IS LIVE RATHER THAN LATENT: `PAYLOAD_KEYS["approval.decide"]` (daemon-command-registry.ts:98) is `["activation","command","graphRevisionRef","record","runId"]`. `approvalPolicy` is NOT allow-listed, and the seam refuses a payload carrying a disallowed key rather than trusting it (:194). So `value === undefined` is ALWAYS true, and `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` is the policy for EVERY gate-free approval decision the daemon makes today — proceed without a human, immediately, with a delay nobody stated.

That is verbatim what `@moe/core`'s own contract comment (approval-policy.ts:47-52) says the contract exists to prevent: "An auto-approval delay that defaults implicitly is the incident's actual mechanism: that board ran a 2s auto-approval nobody had stated per unit of work. A policy that cannot be constructed without naming its delay cannot hide one." The type enforces it; this consumer defeats it with a default.

SECOND, SEPARATE HOLE, currently unreachable but one allow-list edit from live: the caller-supplied branch casts an arbitrary object through `as unknown as ApprovalPolicy` with no validation. If `approvalPolicy` were ever allow-listed, a client could self-approve. The plan deletes the branch rather than relying on a guard in a different file.

THE CONTRACT TO TYPE AGAINST, all published from `@moe/core` (index.ts:144-155): `APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS` = ["PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN","REQUIRE_HUMAN"] (approval-policy.ts:36); `ApprovalPolicy` as a mapped type whose PROCEED arm requires `delayMs` (:58); `ApprovalAuthorityRequest` = `{gate, policy}` (:62); `ApprovalAuthorityDecision` = `{ok, delayMs, grant}` (:68); `decideApprovalAuthority` (:127). Gate handling is already correct and must not move: a satisfied gate proceeds at `delayMs: 0` carrying the grant, and satisfying a gate takes a named human principal so it is not a policy value.

THE TIMER INVERSION, documented at approval-policy.ts:69-77: `delayMs` is a safe non-negative integer, WIDER than `setTimeout` accepts; above 2**31-1 it clamps to 1ms, so a consumer meaning "effectively never" that passes it straight to a timer gets "immediately". The contract explicitly says to bound it at the consumer. This is the nastiest failure mode here because it turns the most conservative configuration into the most permissive one.

RULED OUT AND NOT RE-DERIVED, per the reopenReason: `ProjectConfigurationSettings` (project-configuration-contract.ts:154) and `WrapperKnobs` (wrapper-knobs.ts:9) carry no approval mode. The daemon's established config precedent is env-shaped — `readStoreDependencyEnv` (daemon-store-dependencies.ts:45) and `readWrapperKnobs` — so the loader should follow it rather than invent a mechanism.
planningNotes.risks:
1) THE REGRESSION TEST MUST FAIL BEFORE THE FIX. Step 3(a) asserts that gate-free work does not auto-proceed without authorising settings. Today it does. If that test passes against current HEAD, it is not exercising the defect and the whole task could complete having changed nothing meaningful. Verify the red before implementing; drill 1 re-proves it after.

2) THE DEFENSIVE DEFAULT IS THE DEFECT. Every instinct says "fall back to something sensible when settings are unreadable". Here the only safe fallback is `REQUIRE_HUMAN`. A permissive default is precisely the incident the core contract was written against.

3) THE TIMER INVERSION. A delay above 2**31-1 clamps to 1ms in `setTimeout`, turning "effectively never" into "immediately". Bound it where the timer lives, and require drill 3's red to land on the inversion rather than on a merely wrong number.

4) DELETING VS DISABLING THE PAYLOAD PATH. Leaving it unreachable keeps the authority guarantee in a different file from the handler. Delete `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_POLICY` and `approvalPolicy(payload)` outright; drill 4 re-adds a payload read and requires the handler-level assertion to redden.

5) A PER-CASE REFUSAL LIST CAN BE EXTENDED PERMISSIVELY AND STAY GREEN. Assert "no input yields PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN without a stated delay" as a property over the whole swept set, with a positive generated-case count; drill 5 proves the property is a real sweep.

6) DO NOT DISTURB THE GATE PATH. A satisfied human gate proceeds at `delayMs: 0` carrying its grant, and that is not a policy value. The loaded policy must not change it.

7) DAEMON GATES RED AT BASELINE from foreign slices. Record the before-set; only the delta over the owned files must be empty. Read the count line — exit 0 with no count line ran nothing.

8) SHARED WORKTREE. Re-check `git status --porcelain` before committing, commit by explicit pathspec, verify with `git show --stat`, confirm every drill reverted — drills 1-5 edit production files.

9) REPORTING: the completion should state the defect closed, not just the loader added. "Before this task every gate-free approval decision used `{kind:'PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN', delayMs:0}`" is the finding QA should verify; a completion that only claims "loader landed" understates what changed and makes the regression test look optional.
